sentences.text: Despite popular casts in museums worldwide, Dromaeosaurus is actually poorly known from real fossil evidence and is known from surprisingly few actual fossils.
Researchers estimated Dromaeosaurus had a bite nearly three times stronger than Velociraptor's, suggesting it relied more on its jaws than its sickle claw for killing prey.

The type species Dromaeosaurus albertensis was described by William Diller Matthew and Barnum Brown in 1922 after the first remains were found by Barnum Brown in 1914 near the Red Deer River in Alberta.
Dromaeosaurus used a characteristic 'puncture and pull' feeding method typical of coelurosaurian theropods.

Studies suggest Dromaeosaurus included bone in its diet and was better adapted to attack struggling prey compared to troodontids that ate softer animals and carrion, while the same study indicated that both Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes likely included bone in their diet.
In 1969, John H. Ostrom assigned Dromaeosaurus to the family Dromaeosauridae based on shared features with Velociraptor and Deinonychus.
Teeth attributed to Dromaeosaurus have been found in the Prince Creek Formation.
